topic: Instrument Symbols, Controls, Ranges and Precautions
title: Reading the Dial Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav turns the dial of his meter: a V with a straight line, a V with a wavy line, A, omega, and numbers like 2, 20 and 200. What do all these markings mean? In this animated lesson we decode the symbols on a meter (DC volts, AC volts, amperes, ohms), the sockets (black lead in COM, red lead in the volts and ohms socket, a separate socket for large currents) and the circuit symbols for a voltmeter, an ammeter and a galvanometer.

On a live breadboard a 9 V battery is measured on the 2 V range (O L, over the limit), the 20 V range (9.00) and the 200 V range (9.0), while the oscilloscope's volts per division knob moves the same 9 V line from off the screen to 1.8 divisions. We read an analogue scale step by step (reading = d/N x range), work out a full example (6.4 V), and list the five precautions: highest range first, DC polarity, resistance only with the power off, no parallax, dial to OFF. Then the exam trap (O L does not mean broken), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 23 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
